To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adaptation currents and dynamic thresholds have distinct effects on the f-I curve, and that these effects can be used to distinguish the underlying mechanisms.
adaptation currents and dynamic thresholds produce qualitatively different effects on the transfer function of a neuron and thus should be used in different situations.
the effects of adaptation on a neuron's transfer function strongly depend on the adaptation mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the spike-frequency adaptation of a neuron affects the transfer function of the neuron and how the transfer function of a neuron can be measured in vivo.
the question how adaptation currents or dynamic threshold currents affect the transfer function of neurons.
the effects of adaptation currents on neuronal dynamics and their comparison with dynamic thresholds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a dynamic threshold is not the only way to incorporate spike-frequency adaptation in neuron models, and that a dynamic threshold should be considered only when the effects of adaptation on the f-I curve cannot be reproduced by adaptation currents.

, if a neuron is known to have an adaptation current, then it should be modeled with such an adaptation current, whereas if it does not have such a current, then the neuron's dynamics should be modeled with an adapting threshold.

adaptation currents should be used to model adaptation mechanisms that affect the input-output relationship, while a dynamic threshold should be used when the effect of adaptation is to change the threshold itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adaptation currents act linearly, whereas dynamic thresholds act nonlinearly, and that both can reproduce the observed properties of spike-frequency adaptation in neurons.
adaptation currents are more likely to be modeled by a dynamic threshold, whereas dynamic thresholds are more likely to result from adaptation currents.
the effects of adaptation on the onset fI curves can help to distinguish between different adaptation currents and to identify new mechanisms of adaptation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modeling choice between an adaptation current and a dynamic threshold is crucial and should be guided by experimental data.

, for the analysis of spike-frequency adaptation, the choice between adaptation currents and dynamic thresholds is not a matter of taste but has important consequences for the resulting neuronal signal processing properties.
a neuron's adaptation properties can be inferred by comparing the onset f-I curves measured in different adaptation states.
